original_question: Let f : PN → PN be a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 defined over Q, and let P ∈ PN (Q) be a point whose f -orbit Of (P ) is Zariski dense in PN . Then for every ǫ > 0, the set of primes p : #Of˜(P̃ mod p) ≥ p(1/2−ǫ)N is a set of density 1. 29This conjecture should probably be viewed as a provocation. A safer formulation would be to phrase it as the problem of classfiying all maps for which the conjecture fails to be true!.
target_in_paper: Section 18 (“Dynamics over Finite Fields”), Conjecture 18.3(a), together with its cautionary footnote 29; the draft is not targeting the later upper-bound Question 18.5.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the formal core of Conjecture 18.3(a): a morphism f: P^N -> P^N of degree d >= 2 over Q, a rational point P in P^N(Q) whose forward orbit is Zariski dense, the quantifier 'for every ε > 0', the lower bound of size about p^((1/2-ε)N) for the reduced orbit modulo p, and the conclusion that the relevant primes have density 1. It also reproduces the paper’s cautionary footnote that the conjecture is intended somewhat provocatively.
missing_details: The exact target is Conjecture 18.3(a) in Section 18; the sentence about 'classifying all maps for which the conjecture fails' is footnote 29, not part of the formal conjecture.
The notation O_f(P) should be defined explicitly as the forward orbit {f^n(P) : n >= 0}.
The reductions \tilde{P} and \tilde{f} modulo p should be defined explicitly, following Definitions 12.1 and 12.2; writing 'P̃ mod p' is redundant once \tilde{P} is introduced.
The meaning of 'density 1' should be made explicit as natural density of primes, as in Definition 3.1.
The growth condition should be written unambiguously as p^((1/2-ε)N), not as 'p(1/2-ε)N'.
To be fully stand-alone, the ambient parameter N >= 1 should be stated explicitly.

It helps to note that Proposition 12.5 supplies the nearby context explaining that, for all but finitely many primes of good reduction, reduction and iteration are compatible; those finitely many exceptional primes do not affect a density-1 statement.
The draft should avoid drifting into the different neighboring problem, Question 18.5, which asks for an upper bound #O_{\tilde f}(\tilde P) <= p^((1/2+ε)N) for density-1 many primes.
refined_question:
Let N >= 1 and d >= 2. Let f: P^N -> P^N be a morphism of degree d defined over Q, and let P ∈ P^N(Q) have Zariski-dense forward orbit O_f(P) = {f^n(P) : n >= 0}. For each prime p, let \tilde{P} ∈ P^N(F_p) be the reduction of P modulo p and let \tilde{f}: P^N(F_p) -> P^N(F_p) be the reduction of f modulo p. Is it true that for every ε > 0, the set of primes p such that #O_{\tilde f}(\tilde P) >= p^((1/2-ε)N) has natural density 1; equivalently, that
lim_{X->∞} #{p <= X : #O_{\tilde f}(\tilde P) >= p^((1/2-ε)N)} / #{p <= X : p prime} = 1?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim rendering of Conjecture 18.3(a) in Section 18, and it even includes the accompanying footnote 29 warning that the conjecture is meant as a provocation. The surrounding paper context needed to make it fully stand-alone comes from Section 2 (orbit notation), Section 3 (natural density, projective-space notation, and morphisms), and Section 12 (reduction modulo p for points and maps, plus Proposition 12.5 on compatibility of reduction with iteration at primes of good reduction). Section 18 then states Conjecture 18.3(a), followed immediately by footnote 29 and then Theorem 18.4, which gives only much weaker known lower bounds. Because your draft asks for the lower-bound density-1 statement with exponent (1/2-ε)N, it is clearly aiming at Conjecture 18.3(a), not at Question 18.5, which asks the opposite upper-bound classification problem.
